In the second stage, deep reinforcement learning is used to accurately relocate operations based on repair heuristics to achieve global optimization. A knowledge sharing pattern across scenarios is developed to enhance the generality of the algorithm. Comprehensive experiments on benchmark extensions demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms widely used multi-objective meta-heuristic algorithms while significantly reducing computation time.

Title: Improved variable neighborhood search for the min-degree constrained minimum spanning tree problem
Authors: Manisha Israni, Shyam Sundar
Abstract: The min-degree constrained minimum spanning tree (MDMST) problem is a well-known NP[jls-end-space/]-hard problem of finding a minimum-csot spanning tree while ensuring that every non-leaf vertex has degree at least d[jls-end-space/], where d is a constant positive integer. Degree constraints fundamentally reshape the feasible search space, often forcing the inclusion of longer edges to restore feasibility, which makes the problem particularly challenging. Based on these observations, this paper proposes an improved variable neighborhood search algorithm, denoted as (Formula presented), for the MDMST problem. Unlike the four existing VNS variants, which rely on random edge modifications, the proposed approach incorporates four structurally diverse, degree-based neighborhoods (N1 to N4[jls-end-space/]) that explicitly target edge modification associated with degree-critical vertices. These neighborhoods, combined with tailored local search strategies, enable more effective exploration and refinement of feasible solutions by balancing diversification and intensification in the search space. Extensive experimental analysis confirms the superiority of (Formula presented) over previous four variable neighborhood search variants. Its performance is also superior to state-of-the-art approaches particularly on instances of larger size. (Formula presented) discovers new best-known values on 43 out of 105 instances across all four data-sets, underscoring its capability to explore the search space effectively. Also, (Formula presented) requires only 2 tunable parameters, compared to 12 in the recent approach (Wu et al., 2025), highlighting its robustness and practical efficiency.

Title: Reinforcement learning-guided multi-objective particle swarm optimization with adaptive topology
Authors: Baotong Wu, Zhixiang Chen, Emrah Demir
Abstract: Multi-objective optimization problems often involve a trade-off between convergence toward the Pareto front and diversity along the front. This study proposes a reinforcement learning-guided multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm, called RL-MOPSO, which uses adaptive topology selection to manage this trade-off during the search. The algorithm combines three network topologies: global best, dual-population ring, and Von-Neumann topology with an adaptive jump collaboration operator. Q-learning selects among these topologies dynamically using feedback from convergence and distribution metrics. Computational experiments compare RL-MOPSO with 11 algorithms, including six state-of-the-art methods and five topology-based MOPSO variants. The results show that RL-MOPSO improves both convergence and diversity. The ablation experiments further confirm the contributions of Q-learning and the proposed topology structures.

Title: Conflict-aware seat assignment in classroom environments
Authors: Bruna Cristina Braga Charytitsch, Mariá Cristina Vasconcelos Nascimento
Abstract: Determining an effective seating plan is a key challenge in classroom management, as the spatial arrangement of students directly influences interpersonal dynamics and the overall learning environment. This paper introduces the Student Seat Allocation Problem (SSAP), which consists of strategically assigning students to seats in a traditional classroom, to minimize interpersonal conflicts while satisfying operational constraints. We propose a mathematical model and an Iterated Local Search (ILS) heuristic to address the SSAP. Computational experiments on a benchmark of 131 instances show that both methods converge to the optimal solution in 78 small- and medium-scale instances. For large-scale instances, Gurobi frequently exceeded the time limit, yet achieved very low optimality gaps, outperforming the heuristic’s average gap in 45 instances. ILS, in turn, outperformed Gurobi in 8 instances, and, when analyzing individual runs, successfully reached a gap of zero in multiple executions for several large-scale instances — within a fraction of Gurobi’s computational time. These results position ILS as an effective and accessible alternative for educational institutions where commercial solver licenses are unavailable or cost-prohibitive.

Title: Research on multi-resource flexible job shop scheduling considering flexible matching of pallets and workbenches
Authors: Zhifeng Liu, LinJing Wang, Jun Yan, Yueze Zhang, Yanhong Cheng, Qiang Cheng
Abstract: Pallets and workbenches are one of the main factors affecting production efficiency in multi resource flexible production during the preparation phase. The flexible matching of pallets and workbenches is key issue and directly affects production scheduling. For this purpose, a flexible job shop scheduling model is developed to address multi-stage operations involving setup, processing, and unloading, incorporating specific constraints on workbenches and pallets. An improved genetic algorithm for multi-stage resource-driven scheduling (IGA-MSRDS) is proposed, featuring three-layer encoding, dynamic optimization strategies, and resource-sensitive operators. The algorithm enhances task sequencing and resource coordination through cooperative crossover and load-aware mutation, and refines multi-resource handling via dynamic strategies. The experimental results of multiple benchmark instances demonstrate that IGA-MSRDS excels in scheduling performance. Especially in terms of solution quality and system adaptability under complex resource constraints.

Title: HELP-RL: Real-time policy optimization with hierarchical decoder for heterogeneous and stochastic disaster response logistics
Authors: Hadi Aghazadeh, Xin Wang
Abstract: Disaster response logistics plays a vital role in reducing existential risk in relief operations by ensuring that essential resources reach affected communities promptly during emergencies. Although its significance is widely recognized, existing studies tend to focus primarily on pre-disaster planning, leaving notable gaps in addressing the complex, dynamic, and unpredictable challenges of real-time disaster response. This paper introduces a new framework called HELP-RL ( Humanitarian Emergency Logistics Planning with Reinforcement Learning ) to address these challenges, which are grouped into three main categories: heterogeneous fleet types, diverse demand types, and stochastic travel times. Together, these reflect the real-world complexities of disaster response logistics, all of which require real-time management. The HELP-RL framework incorporates a unique hierarchical decoder to manage the intricate action space, paired with an efficiently designed attention-based policy optimizer using the REINFORCE algorithm. This fully integrated model is built to adapt dynamically to changing disaster conditions, providing reliable and real-time solutions. To assess its performance, we tested the framework using both synthetic and real-world data from wildfire response logistics, drawing on actual data to replicate realistic scenarios. The findings show that HELP-RL produces adaptable and optimal policies that effectively handle rapid changes, surpassing other reinforcement learning approaches in terms of both efficiency and practical applicability.

Title: On disperse generalized linear models
Authors: Emilio Carrizosa, Renato De Leone, Marica Magagnini
Abstract: Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) are a key tool in Explainable Machine Learning, since they provide an easy-to-understand explanation of their coefficients and the impact of the different features in predictions. However, not all accurate GLMs may be equally appealing due to presence of secondary objectives such as sparsity or other measurement costs. For this reason, several methods have been proposed in the literature to address the multiobjective problem of joint optimization of accuracy and other secondary criteria, sparsity being the most popular objective if explainability is pursued. In this work we explore how different GLMs with good accuracy can be. We consider a biobjective P -Dispersion Problem, in which P models are sought jointly maximizing an overall accuracy measure as well as a dispersion measure. Several metrics are used to measure dispersion, such as a function of the distance between their parameters or the set of features used to predict. Moreover, different scenarios for the feasible region are considered, e.g., whether the P models are to be chosen from, or added to, a list of pre-selected GLMs. All these variants are expressed as biobjective nonlinear mixed integer optimization problems. Numerical tests are also presented, showing the effectiveness and the relevance of the proposed methodology.

Title: Instance scaling and metamodel-based sensitivity analysis for rolling horizon optimization with application to postal letter delivery services
Authors: Fabian Dunke, Stefan Nickel
Abstract: In many real-world planning settings, optimization problems are not only large in scale but also must be solved repeatedly as new data becomes available — most notably in rolling horizon schemes. However, this repeated solution process can quickly become computationally prohibitive, especially when assessing the sensitivity of outcomes to model parameters. We address this challenge by integrating two complementary methodological components: First, we propose an instance scaling technique using approximate linear scaling, which systematically reduces problem size to ensure computational tractability with limited loss of solution fidelity. Second, we develop a metamodel-based sensitivity analysis that efficiently displays the relationship between model parameters and solution process outcomes. Using surrogate models such as regression and neural networks, this approach enables fast estimation of both local and global sensitivities, even in complex sequential optimization processes where direct evaluation would require excessive computational effort. Together, these methodological advances form the foundation of a framework for efficiently analyzing the input–output relationships of optimization models used in rolling-horizon schemes. From a practical perspective, the framework enables informed decision-making through systematic alignment of strategic parameter setting in accordance with operational performance. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated for the postal letter delivery services, where it is used to examine the influence of different strategic measures, such as requiring specific delivery service levels or (dis-)incentivizing postponed and express deliveries, upon actual postal operations.

Title: A dual GCN–MCTS framework for yield-aware scheduling in multistage manufacturing
Authors: Sugyeong Lee, Dong-Hee Lee
Abstract: Yield in semiconductor manufacturing is strongly path-dependent, as lots processed through different machine sequences can achieve substantially different final yields even under comparable throughput conditions. Yet conventional scheduling research has focused almost exclusively on productivity metrics, leaving quality-aware scheduling largely unexplored. This paper proposes a dual Graph Convolutional Network (GCN)-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) framework for yield-aware scheduling in a multistage manufacturing process with parallel machines, where the objective is to maximize product yield while preserving production throughput. The framework integrates two complementary GCN components—a Regression GCN (RegGCN) that learns a path-to-yield value function from historical path-yield records, and a Policy GCN (PolGCN), trained through offline policy distillation from RegGCN, that provides state-conditioned action priors over feasible machine assignments for MCTS under real-time machine availability. These components are integrated into a Progressive Value Integration PUCT (PVI-PUCT) selection mechanism that adaptively blends RegGCN value estimates with simulation statistics as tree search matures, enabling informed decisions from the earliest search iterations. Experiments are conducted on a simulated semiconductor dataset incorporating machine-level main effects and adjacent-stage interaction effects that preclude purely additive yield prediction. Results show that RegGCN achieves an R2 of 0.9984 using only 5% of all feasible paths, and that the proposed framework improves yield by +11.18 percentage points over a random baseline while maintaining comparable throughput, matching the performance of parameter-tuned heuristics without requiring sensitivity analysis or parameter selection. The analysis further reveals that the GCN value function provides the primary yield-improvement signal, while MCTS lookahead prevents throughput degradation by accounting for future machine availability in early dispatching decisions. These results demonstrate that process-path data can be transformed into actionable scheduling decisions for yield improvement without requiring additional sensors or inline inspection data.

Title: A batch approximate evaluation method for neighborhood solutions in job shop scheduling
Authors: Zhiyong Ba, Jinduo Liu, Yiping Yuan
Abstract: Efficient neighborhood evaluation is critical for local search in the Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSP). To address the high evaluation cost and strong computational redundancy in neighborhood evaluation, this paper focuses on the well-known N7 neighborhood and proposes a slack-time–based batch approximate evaluation method. The method constructs a slack-time recursion model to enable independent updates of operation head and tail lengths during evaluation. Based on domain knowledge of different N7 move types, a structured batch evaluation framework is further developed, reducing the complexity of batch approximate evaluation to linear time. Computational results show that the proposed method maintains high accuracy, achieves substantial speedups over classical and improved Balas-based evaluations as well as low-thread parallel Balas implementations, and improves the search performance of tabu search.

Title: Budget allocation via data-driven distributionally robust probability maximization
Authors: Belleh Fontem
Abstract: This paper studies a data-driven distributionally robust probability maximization problem arising in risk-averse budget allocation with binary random outcomes and concave response functions. The decision-maker seeks to allocate a limited budget across multiple endeavors to maximize the worst-case probability that the aggregate return exceeds a prescribed threshold. Because the underlying joint success probabilities are unknown, we construct an ambiguity set around the empirical distribution using a total-variation radius calibrated to achieve a certain finite-sample guarantee. The resulting optimization problem is a distributionally robust chance-constrained mixed-binary nonlinear program, which is nonconvex and generally intractable. We obtain structural results that transform the problem into a hierarchy of convex programs. Specifically, we derive a tight linear-programming upper bound on the optimal probability, characterize the critical budget at which this bound becomes attainable, and establish an exact equivalence between the original nonconvex formulation and a parameterized family of surrogate convex programs. These insights enable an exact decomposition algorithm based on nested bisection, which solves the original problem to global optimality through repeated convex optimization. Computational experiments on a real-world marketing application and on synthetic instances demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed approach. The distributionally robust solutions exhibit significantly improved out-of-sample reliability relative to the sample average approximation, particularly in high-dimensional settings and under strictly concave response functions. The results highlight the importance of distributional robustness in data-scarce environments and illustrate how response-function structure and problem scale shape the benefits of robust decision-making.

Title: Optimization on multiple-time reentrant process of robotic cluster tools with parallel process modules and chamber cleaning operations
Authors: YiMing Lai, YongHua Shao, Mohammadhossein Ghahramani, YunFang He, Yan Qiao
Abstract: In a cluster tool, for reentrant processes, wafers need to visit some process modules (PMs) multiple times and cleaning operations are required by PMs to eliminate the residual gases and chemicals, which complicates the scheduling problem of a cluster tool. This work aims to solve the challenging scheduling problem of dual-arm cluster tools with parallel PMs and chamber cleaning operations for reentrant processes. To do so, by analyzing the evolution processes of a tool, it is found that such a tool can operate under a periodical robot task sequence containing several local and global cycles. Furthermore, starting from different legal initial states, the tool can operate under different periodical schedules with different performance in terms of the cycle time. Also, the cycle time can be reduced by minimizing the maximal number of consecutive local cycles in a periodical schedule. With such findings, a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) model is established to minimize the maximum consecutive local cycles by ignoring the chamber cleaning operations. Compared with the existing MILP model to find a global optimal solution, the number of discrete variables in the established MILP is reduced by at least 99.08%, resulting in fast computation. Further, with the chamber cleaning operations considered, based on the established MILP, an efficient two-step method is presented to find the best periodical schedule among various possible robot task sequences. As demonstrated by experimental results, the proposed method is practically applicable since its solution time is less than 2 s in the tested cases.

Title: Reinforcement learning-driven dynamic threshold search for the uncapacitated r-allocation p-hub center problem
Authors: Yongliang Lu, Jinjie Fan, Xinmeng Lin, Shaowen Lan, Mingjie Li, Raymond Chiong
Abstract: The uncapacitated r[jls-end-space/]-allocation p[jls-end-space/]-hub center problem generalizes both the single and multiple allocation p[jls-end-space/]-hub center problems and has numerous applications in transportation networks. The goal of this problem is to identify p hubs and assign each non-hub node to at most r hubs, while minimizing the maximum transportation cost between any pair of nodes. This paper introduces an effective reinforcement learning-driven dynamic threshold search algorithm to solve the problem. The algorithm incorporates a Q-learning-driven solution construction procedure that effectively directs the search toward promising areas, along with a dynamic threshold search that alternates between threshold-based exploration and descent-based improvement to improve solutions. Moreover, novel node-to-hub assignment neighborhoods are designed by modifying only the hub assignments of the critical pair. To further enhance computational efficiency, two fast evaluation strategies are implemented to accelerate the assessment of neighboring solutions. Extensive experiments on two groups of 51 large and challenging benchmark instances demonstrate that the proposed algorithm surpasses state-of-the-art approaches in terms of both solution quality and computational efficiency. In particular, it achieves superior results compared to the existing best-known ones for 33 of the 51 instances and matches the best-known outcomes for the others. The influence of key algorithm components on performance is also examined.

Title: Editorial Board
A decision-supported bi-objective genetic algorithm for hybrid flow shop scheduling with learning effects
Authors: Derya Deliktaş, Mahide Doğan
Abstract: Effective scheduling is essential for maintaining competitiveness in modern production environments. This study addresses a hybrid flow shop scheduling (HFSS) problem in a company producing emergency lighting products, where operator skill significantly affects efficiency. A bi-objective mixed-integer linear programming model is developed to minimize makespan and total tardiness under learning effects. To solve the model, a bi-objective genetic algorithm (BOGA) integrated with three scalarization methods — weighted-sum (WSM), Tchebycheff (TSM), and conic (CSM) — is proposed. Performance is evaluated under different learning levels (70%, 80%, 90%) using 21 benchmark instances. The parameters are tuned through the irace method and full factorial design, with the irace yielding superior outcomes. The results show that the CSM-based approach provides better proximity to ideal and reference points at all levels of learning. Finally, the algorithm is validated through a real-world case study, supported by a decision support system for practical implementation.

Title: A two-stage constraint programming-based heuristic for the dual-resource flexible job shop problem
Authors: José L. Andrade-Pineda, D. Canca, Pedro L. Gonzalez-R, M. Calle, José M. Leon-Blanco
Abstract: This paper addresses the Dual-Resource Constrained Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem (DRCFJSP) with heterogeneous labor, arbitrary non-linear job routes, and operation-level flexibility in both machine and worker assignments. These modelling features yield a highly expressive but computationally challenging makespan-minimization problem for which Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) approaches often struggle to find feasible solutions for medium- and large-scale instances. Leveraging the strong performance of Constraint Programming (CP) in complex scheduling, we develop a novel CP formulation solved with IBM ILOG CP Optimizer. To enhance scalability, we propose a hybrid two-layer solution strategy that decomposes the problem into sequential machine- and worker-assignment phases, both relying on the same CP model with distinct parametrizations. The first layer assigns machine under relaxed worker availability, while the second resolves worker allocations via a pseudo-machine FJSP that preserves feasibility through extended technological precedence constraints. Experiments on a new benchmark of 52 DRCFJSP instances, derived from a well-known FJSP dataset, show that the proposed method significantly outperforms the direct application of the CP model in both time and solution quality.

Title: Rationalizing dense road sensor networks for traffic state Reconstruction: a probabilistically constrained surrogate optimization framework
Authors: Junli Liu, Yanzhan Chen, Ruiguang Liu, Liang Zheng
Abstract: Dense traffic sensor networks often contain substantial information redundancy, leading to unnecessary data processing, communication, and maintenance costs. This study investigates how to rationalize an already deployed sensor network while preserving its capability for network-wide traffic state reconstruction. We propose a Road Sensor Location Model for Network-wide Traffic State Reconstruction (RSLM-NTSR), formulated as a probabilistically constrained stochastic black-box optimization model that minimizes the expected Reconstruction Error of Network-wide Traffic State (RE-NTS) while controlling the risk of excessive Maximum Reconstruction Error of Road Traffic State (MRE-RTS). To make the problem computationally tractable, a Spatio-Temporal Spectral Clustering (STSC) algorithm is first developed to identify redundant sensors and transform the original high-dimensional binary pruning problem into a lower-dimensional representative sensor selection problem. A Self-Attention Graph Convolution Reconstruction Network (SAGCRN) is then used as an expensive simulation-based evaluator to assess each sensor retention scheme. To solve the resulting large-scale integer black-box optimization problem, we propose a Parameterized Gaussian Process Belief-based Rapid Knowledge Gradient (PGPB-RKG) algorithm, which integrates a structured Gaussian process belief model, a Latent-space Variance Estimation Network (LaVEnt), and a Rapid Knowledge Gradient (RKG) sampling policy. Numerical experiments on a Los Angeles freeway network with 593 sensors show that the proposed framework reduces the retained sensor set to 140 representative sensors while achieving an average RE-NTS of 6.41% and satisfying the probabilistic MRE-RTS constraint. Comparative experiments against representative heuristic, metaheuristic, and Bayesian optimization baselines demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed optimization algorithm. These results indicate that reconstruction-oriented sensor rationalization can substantially reduce sensing redundancy while maintaining reliable network-wide traffic state observability.

Title: Breaking hierarchical silos in multi-project dedicated staffing: A nested optimization approach
Authors: Yaohui Liu, Ronggui Ding, Chen Cheng, Lei Wang
Abstract: Motivated by the management practices of concurrent high-end equipment research and development projects, this paper introduces a multi-project dedicated staffing problem (MPDSP) to ensure project execution efficiency and avoid organizational disturbances. A major challenge arises from the hierarchical silos separating the resource manager and project managers, resulting in information asymmetry that hinders alignment between project requirements and the skill sets of assigned personnel. For this, we develop an optimization-based hierarchical decision framework for the MPDSP that breaks down decision silos through bidirectional feedback between global staffing and local scheduling. Local scheduling supports global staffing by identifying critical skills and generating a broader range of candidate solutions. Solving the optimization problem is challenged by its inherently NP-hardness and the curse of dimensionality stemming from its nested structure. Therefore, we put forward a metaheuristic-based nested optimization approach with a two-fold design: a novel self-guided neighborhood search mechanism that dynamically steers the search toward high-potential regions and facilitates targeted exploration at the upper level to improve computational efficiency; a tailored algorithm that expands search possibilities at the lower level to avoid local optima and generate more accurate feedback for guiding upper-level decisions. Numerical experiments validate the performance of the proposed approach across various scenarios. Further examination of the optimal solution highlights the importance of considering skill synergy in multi-project staffing and emphasizing diverse roles in intra-project staffing.

Title: The vehicle routing problem with driver scheduling
Authors: Razieh Mousavi, Jean-François Côté, Maryam Darvish
Abstract: This paper addresses the vehicle routing problem with driver scheduling, which involves planning delivery routes while assigning work shifts to drivers whose individual availability must be respected. The problem extends the classical vehicle routing problem by incorporating driver availability, reflecting a growing operational concern in the logistics sector marked by persistent labor shortages and an increased need for flexible work arrangements. A mathematical model is developed to minimize total operational costs, including travel, driver shift, and outsourcing costs when some deliveries are assigned to third-party logistics providers. To handle large instances efficiently, a heuristic based on the Iterated Local Search algorithm is proposed. The algorithm integrates route optimization and driver scheduling decisions within a single framework. Computational experiments show that accounting for driver availability results in significant cost reductions and operational improvements. Even modest increases in driver availability significantly decrease the need for outsourcing, while full-day availability yields only marginal additional savings. These results offer practical managerial insights for logistics planners seeking to create a balance between operational efficiency and workforce constraints, as well as driver well-being.

Title: Robust scheduling policy learning for ore-flow blending in dynamic and uncertain environments
Authors: Hao Tang, Changhe Li, Guoyu Chen, Shoufei Han, Michalis Mavrovouniotis, Miqing Li, Liang Yuan
Abstract: Ore-flow blending is essentially a real-time scheduling decision problem where equipment failures, sudden weather changes, and time-varying road network exist during production. This problem faces core challenges including high-dimensional spatiotemporal dynamics, real-time decision response, and long-horizon decision dependencies. To overcome these challenges, this paper designs an end-to-end ore-flow blending and truck scheduling framework based on a spatio-temporal graph policy network. By encoding the spatial topology of the road network and the dynamic temporal sequences of the ore flow into a unified state representation, the proposed model achieves scalable learning across road networks of varying scales and structures. Furthermore, a two-stage training strategy combining local short-horizon pre-training and global long-horizon fine-tuning is proposed, effectively resolving the computational and memory consumption challenges in large-scale, long-horizon scenarios. Experimental results on multiple real-world mine cases and dynamic scenarios demonstrate that this method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in ore flow stability control and exhibits strong robustness and generalization capabilities under different road network structures, equipment scales, and dynamic events.

Title: Integrating maintenance and scheduling decisions in single-machine systems: insights from a systematic and bibliometric review
Authors: Pravin P. Tambe, Makarand S. Kulkarni, Jiju Antony
Abstract: Proper coordination between scheduling and maintenance activities helps to minimize downtime, ensure efficient resource utilization, and smooth production. Over the past two decades, the joint consideration of maintenance planning with production scheduling in single-machine environments has emerged as an important research area for enhancing operational efficiency and competitiveness in manufacturing. To the best of our knowledge, there is currently no survey focused explicitly on maintenance combined scheduling decisions in the context of single-machine systems. This paper aims to fill this gap by presenting a systematic literature review (SLR) of studies that modelled and solved the combined problem of maintenance and single-machine scheduling. The SLR aims to answer key research questions related to the current state of scientific research, influential publications, modelling approaches, and future research directions. Following a structured review protocol, relevant publications were identified, screened, and analyzed. This study presents a bibliometric analysis to systematically identify and analyze research articles from leading journals in the Scopus and Web of Science (WoS) databases. The study included 174 research articles published in ABDC A*/A/B and SCImago Q1 category journals, as well as selected conference proceedings, to map the research trend over the last 25 years. The selected studies were reviewed and classified under four areas: solution approaches, objective(s), maintenance types, and computing tools applied to solve the problem. A review of the published research highlights that 24.7% of studies used more than one objective, minimizing makespan as the objective used in 22.4% of studies, while minimizing cost (16.6%) was also commonly used, followed by tardiness and completion time. In the maintenance type, preventive maintenance (PM) was the most commonly used approach, found in almost 48.8% of studies. Overall, the review provides a useful reference for researchers and practitioners by outlining major developments, commonly used modeling approaches, and future directions highlighted by the researchers.

Title: Navigating network availability: A shortest path approach to UAV traffic routing
Authors: Nazli Demir, Fatma Gzara
Abstract: The use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), commonly known as drones, is rapidly increasing across both commercial and recreational domains. This growth highlights a significant challenge: the lack of a drone traffic management system with a well-defined airspace traffic network and routing and flight path planning. As drone operations expand, the airspace becomes increasingly crowded, increasing the risk of aerial conflicts and emphasizing the need for effective regulatory and operational frameworks. This research aims to address these challenges by developing tools to be integrated into UAV Traffic Management (UTM) systems, enabling efficient flight planning for UAVs within an airspace structured as a network, in consideration of ongoing traffic. A novel mathematical model is proposed to find a flight plan that specifies the flight path as well as a time schedule of traversing arcs on the path, while accounting for battery capacity limitations. A network transformation method is developed to reformulate the problem on an auxiliary network that allows solution by a novel labeling algorithm. Extensive computational experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms a commercial solver and is capable of solving large-scale instances in under two seconds, making it highly suitable for seamless integration into UTM systems. The results further provide insights into how traffic density, route length, and battery capacity interact to shape route feasibility and arrival performance. These findings highlight key trade-offs relevant to UTM design and support the development of traffic-aware and energy-conscious flight planning tools for UAV operations.

Title: Integrating performance metrics for multi-objective optimization: a case study with MOEAs
Authors: Shuqi Xu, Jinghe Sun, Zhiyang Shen, Majid Eskandarpour
Abstract: The rapid development of multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) has been accompanied by a proliferation of performance metrics, each designed to capture different aspects of algorithmic performance. However, relying on a single metric often provides an isolated perspective, and the choice of metric can bias the evaluation, potentially leading to conclusions stuck in a “local optimum.” To overcome these limitations, this study introduces a novel Multi-Criteria Performance Indicator (MCPI) that integrates multiple existing metrics into a unified analytical framework. Within this framework, we model each algorithm as a decision-making unit and employ a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) approach to construct a Pareto-optimal best-performance frontier. The proposed MCPI is derived from the relative distance of each algorithm to this frontier, integrating multiple performance aspects into a single, comprehensive measure. Extensive experiments on 21 representative MOEAs validate the effectiveness and discriminative power of MCPI.

Title: Double-layer Benders decomposition for large-scale robust uncapacitated hub location
Authors: Haifeng Zhang, Jian-Cai Wang, Yuan Gao
Abstract: This paper models the robust counterpart for uncapacitated hub location problem with multiple assignments (UHLP), which simultaneously considers uncertainties associated with setup costs and flow amounts. A strong and tractable mixed-integer linear programming formulation is proposed, which can be reformulated in a Benders decomposition fashion, and a double-layer Benders decomposition algorithm is developed to efficiently solve large-scale instances of the problem. In the first layer, we propose a Benders decomposition algorithm to solve the LP relaxation of the master problem, obtaining a pool of valid optimality cuts; in the second layer, we exploit the obtained cuts to warm up the Benders decomposition algorithm on the master problem. In each of the two Benders decomposition algorithms, we design tailored efficient methods to exactly solve the subproblems and develop effective cuts refinement skills to generate strong optimality cuts. Extensive computational experiments are performed on well-known instances with up to 500 nodes to investigate the effect of incorporating uncertainty and verify the superior performance of the proposed solution method.

Title: Data-driven interdiction with asymmetric cost uncertainty: A distributionally robust optimization approach
Authors: Sergey S. Ketkov, Oleg A. Prokopyev
Abstract: We consider a class of stochastic interdiction games between an upper-level decision-maker (the leader) and a lower-level decision-maker (the follower), where uncertainty lies in the follower's objective function coefficients. Specifically, the follower's profits (or costs) in our model comprise a random vector, whose probability distribution is estimated independently by the leader and the follower, based on their own data. To address the distributional uncertainty, we formulate a distributionally robust interdiction (DRI) model, where both decision-makers solve conventional distributionally robust optimization problems based on the Wasserstein metric. For this model, we prove asymptotic consistency and derive a polynomial-size mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) reformulation. Furthermore, in our bilevel optimization context, the leader may face uncertainty due to its incomplete knowledge of the follower's data. In this regard, we propose two distinct approximations of the true DRI model, where the leader has incomplete or no information about the follower's data. The first approach employs a pessimistic approximation, which turns out to be computationally challenging and requires a specialized reformulation amenable to a Benders-type decomposition algorithm. The second approach leverages a robust optimization approach from the leader's perspective. To address the resulting problem, we propose a scenario-based approximation that admits a potentially large single-level MILP reformulation and satisfies asymptotic robustness guarantees. Finally, for a class of randomly generated instances of the packing interdiction problem, we evaluate numerically how the information asymmetry and the decision-makers' risk preferences affect the models' out-of-sample performance.

Title: Resilience enhancement in power distribution systems: Chance-constrained model with decision-dependent atoms
Authors: P. Dehghanian, M.A. Lejeune, J. Su, Z. Wang
Abstract: Mobile power sources (MPSs) offer considerable promise to facilitate the exchange of spatiotemporal flexibility in the power distribution system (PDS) and enhance its resilience to extreme emergencies. The service restoration process can be made more efficient by strategically prepositioning MPSs in advance of and allocating them during high-impact low-probability extremes. This paper introduces a new decision-dependent chance-constrained model, where the atoms of the probability distribution of a random variable are distorted by decisions. The model is designed to address the service restoration problem in PDSs and optimize the pre-disaster deployment of MPSs. The proposed service restoration scheme is formulated as a mixed-integer joint chance-constrained model with nonconvex continuous relaxation. We develop an efficient method to reformulate the chance-constrained model with decision-dependent uncertainty as an equivalent mixed-integer linear problem. Case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed restoration scheme in boosting PDS resilience and the significance of incorporating endogenous uncertainties in the service restoration process.

Title: A parallel branch-and-bound-and-check algorithm for nesting
Authors: Juan J. Lastra-Díaz, M. Teresa Ortuño
Abstract: The irregular strip packing problem, also known as nesting, involves computing a non-overlapping placement of a set of polygons onto a rectangular strip of fixed width and minimum length. Recent performance gains in Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) solvers have encouraged the proposal of exact optimization models for nesting. The Dotted-Board (DB) MILP model solves the discrete version of the problem by constraining the positions of the polygons to lie on a fixed-point grid. However, the number of non-overlapping constraints grows quadratically with the number of dots and polygon types, which has encouraged the proposal of a Clique Covering reformulation (DB-CC), setting the current state-of-the-art by significantly reducing the constraints required. However, DB-CC requires a significant preprocessing time to compute edge and vertex clique coverings. Moreover, current knowledge of the stable set polytope suggests that achieving a tighter formulation is unlikely. Thus, our main hypothesis is that an ad hoc exact algorithm requiring no preprocessing might be a better option to solve the DB model than the costly Branch-and-Cut approach. This work proposes an exact parallel branch-and-bound-and-check algorithm to solve the DB model from the inverse conflict graph, using ad hoc data structures, bounding, and forward-checking to prune the search space. We also introduce a new Lower Bound (LB) algorithm as a by-product. Our experiments show that our algorithm significantly reduces the resolution time compared to DB-CC and eliminates its preprocessing step. Seventeen open instances are solved up to optimality, and our LB algorithm proves the optimality of fifty-one instances.

Title: Metaheuristic approaches for the Manhattan metric straddle carrier routing problem with buffer areas
Authors: Ahmet Cürebal, Nina Radojičić, Leonard Heilig, Stefan Voß
Abstract: This study investigates an optimization problem in container terminals, where straddle carriers (SCs) transport containers between seaside and stacking areas. Container transportation sequences respect both the predetermined loading sequence at quay cranes (QCs) and the capacity restrictions of buffer areas located below QCs for container exchange between SCs and QCs. We propose two sets of strategies. The first prioritizes runtime efficiency, employing methods such as a local search procedure and two variants of Variable Neighborhood Descent. For the second strategy, we use two different metaheuristics, namely Variable Neighborhood Search and a Greedy Randomized Adaptive Search Procedure, to provide solutions with superior objective function values. The performance of these methods is assessed in an extensive computational study and compared with benchmarks from the literature, showing that the proposed methods effectively allocate containers to SCs, resulting in minimized idle times of QCs and, consequently, shorter turnaround times for vessels.

Title: An efficient memetic algorithm for the corridor allocation problem
Authors: Gintaras Palubeckis, Alfonsas Misevičius, Armantas Ostreika
Abstract: This paper addresses the corridor allocation problem (CAP), which consists of arranging n departments along both sides of a corridor without overlap and without gaps between adjacent departments. The CAP arises in facility layout design and is computationally challenging for large-scale instances due to the combinatorial nature of the search space. Despite the progress achieved in recent years, existing solution approaches often struggle to efficiently explore large neighborhoods while maintaining high solution quality. Motivated by these limitations, this study proposes a new memetic algorithm (MA) specifically designed for solving large-scale CAP instances. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm relies on two key methodological contributions: a fast local search (LS) technique and a novel crossover mechanism. The LS procedure constitutes a significant methodological advancement for the CAP, as it enables rapid exploration of the insertion neighborhood of the current solution. The worst-case time complexity of the neighborhood exploration procedure is (Formula presented), where R denotes the ratio between the largest and the smallest department lengths in a dataset. In addition, a new crossover mechanism is introduced that operates on two pairs of permutations through an encoding-decoding scheme, enabling more effective recombination of high-quality solutions. Extensive computational experiments on standard CAP benchmark instances demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed MA compared with state-of-the-art algorithms. The algorithm produced new best-known solutions for 49 benchmark instances. Further experimental analysis shows that the proposed MA is more than n times faster than a variant in which the proposed LS procedure is replaced with the best LS technique reported in recent literature. Additional results also indicate that the proposed crossover mechanism helps to produce significantly better solutions than the crossover operator used in existing genetic algorithms for the CAP.

Title: Modeling and optimization of machine deterioration effects in low-carbon flexible job shop scheduling problems
Authors: Zhuo Su, Junlong Peng, Yuntao Su, Xiao Liu, Chupei Chen
Abstract: With the continuous development of global manufacturing, reducing carbon emissions and energy consumption has become a core challenge. Industrial production accounts for over 30% of global carbon emissions, underscoring the importance of carbon emission optimization in production scheduling. Moreover, machine deterioration effects, particularly during low-load states, significantly affect production efficiency and energy consumption yet are often overlooked in existing literature. To address this, this paper proposes a Low-Carbon Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Optimization Model (LC-FJSP-MDE). The core novelty lies in the explicit quantification of “low-load deterioration” using a time-varying conversion coefficient, bridging the gap between theoretical assumptions and the physical reality of standby wear. To solve this problem, an improved multi-objective optimization algorithm, NSGA-II-IP, is designed. It integrates a dynamic low-carbon decoding strategy, Composite Differential Evolution (CoDE), and Knowledge-Driven Tabu Search (KD-TS) to achieve coordinated global and local optimization. Experimental results demonstrate significant performance gains: on small-scale instances, the proposed algorithm identifies the identical global optimal solutions as the exact solver (Gurobi) while drastically reducing the computational time to mere seconds, exhibiting a superior balance between solution quality and computational efficiency. Furthermore, it outperforms state-of-the-art meta-heuristics and Deep Reinforcement Learning (D3QN) approaches by over 15% in complex scenarios. Finally, a real-world automotive case study validates its practicability. Furthermore, this study provides practitioners with actionable insights on transitioning from “high-load only” to “full-cycle” maintenance strategies, demonstrating its robust applicability in real production environments.

Title: Enhancing optimization algorithms with Kernel Density Estimation: A statistical learning strategy for smarter metaheuristics
Authors: Daniele Ferone, Paola Festa, Tommaso Pastore
Abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms are commonly used for efficiently solving intractable optimization problems, given their ability to provide solutions while requiring relatively low computational efforts. This paper presents KDE-STOP, a novel strategy based on Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) to improve the efficiency of any target single-solution metaheuristic. In our framework, the algorithm analyzes objective function values attained during its initial iterations to estimate the distribution of encountered solutions. This distribution is then used to evaluate the probability of improving the current best solution, enabling the algorithm to reduce runtimes by terminating its execution as soon as it is unlikely to generate better solutions. The effectiveness of KDE-STOP is validated through experiments on a diverse set of metaheuristic and optimization problems, demonstrating its capability of improving the efficiency and effectiveness of a wide variety of target algorithms.

Title: A discrete differential evolution algorithm for the constrained single-row facility layout problem with asymmetric clearances
Authors: Feristah Ozcelik, Aslihan Karas Celik
Abstract: Facility layout problems (FLPs) require adequate clearances between facilities to ensure operational safety and efficiency. Most studies simplify this issue by assuming fixed or symmetric distances, whereas in real applications clearances are often asymmetric and sequence-dependent. Constrained single-row facility layout problems (cSRFLPs), in turn, incorporate positioning, ordering, and relation constraints. Although both aspects have been investigated separately, no prior study has jointly considered asymmetric clearances within constrained layouts. This paper introduces the cSRFLP with asymmetric clearances and develops a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model to minimise total material-handling cost while explicitly capturing clearance asymmetry and logical constraint structures. For large-scale instances that become computationally intractable for exact optimisation, a discrete differential evolution algorithm (DDEA) with an embedded repair framework is proposed. The algorithm is systematically calibrated using a structured experimental design to determine robust parameter settings across different problem sizes. Computational experiments on newly generated asymmetric-clearance benchmark instances demonstrate the competitiveness and scalability of the proposed approach. Furthermore, when applied to 73 classical cSRFLP benchmark instances, the calibrated DDEA outperformed exact approaches in 17 cases and surpassed the best-known metaheuristic results in 19 others, while matching the remaining solutions. These findings confirm the robustness, scalability, and generalisability of the proposed method.

Title: Efficient mathematical programming formulation and algorithmic framework for optimal camera placement
Authors: Yash Kumar, Raghu Bollapragada, Benjamin D. Leibowicz
Abstract: Optimal camera placement plays a crucial role in applications such as surveillance, environmental monitoring, and infrastructure inspection. Even highly abstracted versions of this problem are NP-hard due to the high-dimensional continuous domain of camera configurations (i.e., positions and orientations) and difficulties in efficiently and accurately calculating camera coverage. In this paper, we present a novel framework for optimal camera placement that uses integer programming and adaptive sampling strategies to maximize coverage, given a limited camera budget. We develop a modified maximum k-coverage formulation and two adaptive sampling strategies, Explore and Exploit (E&E) and Target Uncovered Spaces (TUS), that iteratively add new camera configurations to the candidate set in order to improve the solution. E&E focuses on local search around camera configurations chosen in previous iterations, whereas TUS focuses specifically on covering regions that were previously uncovered. We first conduct theoretical analysis to provide bounds on the probability of finding an optimal solution and expected sampling needs, while ensuring monotonic improvements in coverage. Then, we conduct a detailed numerical analysis over different environments. Results show that E&E achieves coverage improvements of 3.3-16.0% over all baseline random sampling approaches, while maintaining manageable computational times. Meanwhile, TUS performs well in open environments and with tight camera budgets, achieving gains of 6.9-9.1% in such conditions. Compared to the baseline, our approach achieves similar coverage using only 30-70% of the sampling budget, demonstrating its computational efficiency. Through a case study, we obtain insights into optimal camera placement decisions for a typical indoor surveillance application.

Title: Online multi-appointment scheduling for outpatient examinations with genetic programming
Authors: Huan Zhang, Yang Wang, Jin-Kao Hao, Lihui Zeng, Li Luo
Abstract: Centralized appointment platforms in hospitals allow patients to submit their appointment requests online and receive real-time confirmations of available date and time slots, which simplifies the appointment process and reduces the administrative burden. However, existing multi-appointment scheduling systems in hospitals typically rely on simple dispatching rules, which are myopic and insufficient to balance two critical patient needs: minimizing the total number of hospital visits and reducing the number of waiting days. To address this issue, we formulate a novel online multi-appointment scheduling problem (OMASP) that explicitly targets both objectives. Due to the complexity of designing effective dispatching rules manually, we propose a genetic programming (GP) approach to automatically evolve high-performing dispatching rules. The proposed GP framework integrates a multi-fidelity simulation evaluator and a feature selection mechanism to enhance both performance and interpretability. Using real data from a large hospital, we design simulation scenarios that reflect both the number of patient examinations and the daily arrival rates of appointment requests. Computational results show that our proposed GP method achieves an objective improvement of 13.88% compared to baseline methods. The performance gains are particularly pronounced in scenarios with a high average number of examinations per patient and elevated daily request volumes. By analyzing the behavior of the evolved rules through explicit simplification and a new visualization method, we provide valuable managerial implications that can inform and enhance hospital appointment scheduling practices.

Title: Learning to solve single-batch-processing machine scheduling problem with two-dimensional packing constraints
Authors: Fan Wu, Ziming He, Kanxin Hu, Jingwen Li, Haobin Shi
Abstract: Machines that simultaneously process jobs in a batch and sequentially handle batches are widely used in additive manufacturing such as three-dimensional (3D) printing. This paper is concerned with the job packing and batch scheduling problem of single-batch-processing machine under two-dimensional geometric constraints (2D-SBPM). Existing approaches for 2D-SBPM predominantly rely on heuristic methods, which often yield suboptimal solutions due to repetitive evaluation cycles during scheduling and the persistent dependence on conventional heuristic rules for packing. To improve computational efficiency and solution quality, this paper proposes a two-stage solution scheme based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Specifically, we introduce a packing method, called Packing-Net, that significantly enhances the conventional packing scheme by the attention mechanism. Furthermore, we propose a sequence generator with multiple policy optimization to make the training process fast and stable. Directly generating job sequences avoids invalid evaluations. Experimental results show that our method outperforms the conventional heuristics with various sizes.

Title: Integrated E‑waste supply chain optimization via Lagrangian relaxation: shared‑fleet collection, robotic disassembly and redistribution
Authors: Homeyra Kord, Javad Behnamian
Abstract: Technological advances have significantly shortened the life cycle of electronic products, leading to a rapid increase in electronic waste generation. This study develops an integrated reverse logistics (RL) framework for e-waste management that jointly addresses collection, disassembly, and distribution of recovered materials. The proposed model integrates (i) a two-echelon collection system combining internal and shared fleets, (ii) robotic disassembly operation planning with precedence-based sequencing, and (iii) distribution routing of recycled materials to secondary markets. The resulting formulation is expressed as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming model with explicit mass-balance constraints linking all stages of the network. Given the combinatorial complexity and strong coupling among decision layers, a Lagrangian Relaxation (LR) decomposition approach is developed to obtain high-quality solutions within reasonable computational time. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated against the BARON solver implemented in GAMS using 45 randomly generated test instances of varying sizes. Computational results show that, for instances solved to optimality or near-optimality by both methods, the LR approach reduces average computation time by approximately 25–30% compared to the exact solver while maintaining competitive solution quality. In particular, the average optimality gap between the LR heuristic solutions and the best feasible solutions obtained by GAMS is 2.70%, while the average duality gap is 2.39%, indicating the strength of the Lagrangian bounds and the reliability of the decomposition strategy. The average heuristic Lagrangian gap is 5.45%, further confirming the consistency of the proposed approach. For medium- and large-scale instances, the exact solver frequently reaches the predefined computational time limit (18,000 s) without guaranteeing optimality or, in some cases, without returning feasible solutions, whereas the proposed LR algorithm consistently generates feasible and high-quality solutions in significantly shorter computational times. These findings highlight the scalability, computational efficiency, and practical applicability of the proposed framework for large-scale reverse logistics systems in e-waste management.

Title: Integrated production and transportation scheduling under no on-site storage, sequence-dependent setups, and multi-mode transportation
Authors: Boyue Cao, Peng Wu
Abstract: This paper investigates an integrated production and transportation scheduling problem motivated by a real-world application in which finished products must be immediately loaded onto transport vehicles due to the absence of on-site storage, in order to satisfy the demands of off-site warehouses. The problem jointly determines production quantities, production sequencing under sequence-dependent setup times, and the allocation of transportation resources, including pre-reserved trains and flexible trucks. The objective is to minimize the total cost, including inventory holding and backorder costs at the warehouses, as well as fixed and variable transportation costs for both trains and trucks. We formulate the problem as a mixed-integer linear programming model and analyze its structural properties. To solve it effectively and efficiently, we develop a bi-level heuristic algorithm based on these properties. The upper level determines the total number of trucks by using a dichotomy method, while the lower level constructs production and transportation plans under the given truck allocation. Computational results show that the proposed bi-level heuristic provides competitive solutions on both small- and large-scale instances compared with MILP, a genetic algorithm, other existing heuristic methods, and a learning-based approach.

Title: List-based simulated annealing algorithm with novel encoding structure for the bounded diameter minimum spanning tree problem
Authors: Fuyuan Zheng, Ning Li, Kai Yang, Liping Xu, Juan Lin, Yiwen Zhong
Abstract: This paper investigates the Bounded Diameter Minimum Spanning Tree (BDMST) problem, which aims to identify a minimum-cost spanning tree T subject to a specified diameter constraint D[jls-end-space/]. A novel solution representation, termed Level-Based Order Encoding (LBOE), is proposed to represent diameter-constrained trees. Compared to permutation and level encodings, LBOE demonstrates superior representation capability. Theoretical analysis establishes that LBOE effectively addresses the limitations of permutation encoding in representing optimal solutions. Based on this representation, a List-Based Simulated Annealing (LBSA) algorithm is developed to solve the BDMST problem. To facilitate efficient exploration and exploitation of the solution space, a hybrid neighborhood structure — comprising center exchange, swap, and insert operations — is designed to generate neighboring solutions. The performance of the LBSA algorithm is evaluated on 25 challenging Euclidean instances and 20 non-Euclidean instances. The proposed method achieves new best-known solutions for 22 out of 45 instances. Furthermore, results from the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Holm correction indicate that LBSA statistically significantly outperforms six state-of-the-art metaheuristics.

Title: Machine-aligned multi-agent reinforcement learning for dynamic flexible job shop scheduling
Authors: Bi Wang, Le Xia, Yang Chen
Abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for the Dynamic Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem (DFJSP) due to its adaptability and decentralized decision-making. With agent behaviors being unpredictable and the global reward ambiguous, current MARL methods face the challenges of non-stationarity and credit assignment. To address these, we propose a machine-aligned MARL framework for the DFJSP with stochastic job arrivals. An abstract state–action representation, augmented with priority dispatching rules (PDRs), aligns heterogeneous machines at the decision semantics level, enabling a unified policy that promotes more coordinated scheduling behavior. A dense local reward signal combines sparse, unbiased tardiness variations with dense slack values that reflect potential tardiness, yielding a hybrid measure that integrates both realized outcomes and predictive information. Experiments demonstrate that our approach consistently reduces total tardiness by 25.09% compared with classical dispatching rules and by 22.31% compared with RL baselines on average across scenarios, achieving robust online scheduling performance. Furthermore, extensive validation confirms that the proposed reward exhibits a strong and statistically significant negative correlation with total tardiness, demonstrating strong alignment with the scheduling objective.

Title: Online multiple resource allocation problems with departures via the primal–dual approach
Authors: Yusuf Amidu, Khaled Elbassioni, Adriana F. Gabor
Abstract: This paper introduces primal–dual algorithms for several variants of the online resource allocation problem with departures. In the basic setting, requests arrive over time to a set of resources (knapsacks). Upon arrival, each request reveals its duration, demand, and reward. The algorithm must decide immediately whether to accept or reject the request and, if accepted, assign it to a resource to maximize total reward. Under mild assumptions, we show that the primal–dual algorithm achieves the same competitive ratio as a recent threshold-based approach: (Formula presented), where θ̄max is the maximum value density fluctuation ratio and d̄max is the maximum duration fluctuation ratio. We extend this framework to a multi-dimensional variant, where requests consume capacity on multiple resources, and to a novel load-balancing variant. Our results demonstrate that the primal–dual approach provides a simple, unified framework for achieving competitive ratios comparable to those recently obtained in the literature, while allowing extensions to more complex variants such as load balancing, without degrading performance. Through numerical experiments, we show that simple modifications of the primal–dual heuristic can lead to improved empirical competitive ratios in practical settings. Finally, the proposed primal–dual algorithms have significantly lower computation times compared to the threshold counterparts.

Title: The non-disjoint Clustered Traveling Salesperson Problem
Authors: Felix Weidinger, Kris Braekers
Abstract: The traveling salesperson problem (TSP) has a long tradition in Operations Research and, thereby, is still relevant as the core and therefore important subproblem of decision problems in today’s research. However, the TSP in its general form often lacks specific characteristics of the higher-level planning problems. For that reason, many extensions of the TSP have been developed over recent decades, allowing to consider additional constraints. The paper introduces the non-disjoint Clustered Traveling Salesperson Problem (ndCTSP), for which vertices are a member of at least one cluster. Having multiple non-disjoint clusters, a shortest tour is searched for, which enters each cluster at most once and only visits vertices in direct succession if they belong to the same (entered) cluster. Two variants of the problem are introduced, the unlimited and the limited version, for which the number of entered clusters is either unrestricted or bounded by a problem parameter, respectively. Theoretical insights, three different (mixed) integer linear programming formulations, and complexity results are provided. Further, the broad applicability and relevance of the novel problem are indicated by demonstrating how it generalizes three exemplarily selected planning problems from different domains. Computational tests on the solution performance of the proposed modeling approaches are provided for randomized instances to provide an unbiased evaluation. Finally, a first benchmark on structured instances of one of the generalized problems showcases that solving the ndCTSP outperforms specialized mixed integer models described in literature.

Title: Stochastic autonomous vehicle-assisted two-echelon location-routing problem: A logic-based Benders decomposition approach
Authors: Xiaojin Zheng, Xintao Shi, Chenxu Li, Yanxia Zhang, Shengkun Qin
Abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce, combined with persistent labor shortages in urban logistics, has intensified the need for delivery systems that effectively integrate autonomous technologies with human labor. This study investigates a stochastic autonomous vehicle-assisted two-echelon location-routing problem, which can be viewed as a variant of the classical two-echelon location-routing problem in an urban logistics setting. The first stage determines the locations of microhubs and assigns customers to activated hubs, while the second stage optimizes coordinated routing decisions for autonomous vehicles (AVs) and human couriers (HCs) under demand uncertainty. To solve the problem efficiently, we develop a logic-based Benders decomposition (LBBD) algorithm. The second-stage subproblem is optimized via column generation using a newly designed multi-mode set partitioning reformulation that accurately captures the service selection decisions of AVs and HCs. The solution framework is further enhanced with branch-and-price, and valid lower bounds to strengthen computational performance. Computational experiments on small- and medium-scale instances demonstrate that the proposed LBBD framework yields high-quality solutions with significant performance improvements. Sensitivity analyses reveal that the AV-assisted delivery strategy can significantly reduce total delivery costs and alleviate labor shortages by decreasing reliance on HCs.

Title: Simulation-based dynamic optimization for ambulance dispatch and casualty distribution in mass casualty incident
Authors: Kuo-Hao Chang, Tzu-Li Chen, Lan-Hsin Yu, Tzu-Yin Chang
Abstract: After an earthquake, the sudden influx of casualties from multiple zones overwhelms medical resources such as ambulances and hospital beds. This post-disaster mass casualty incident (MCI) is highly unpredictable, with conditions continuously evolving over time, making it urgent to develop real-time and flexible ambulance dispatch and casualty distribution strategies to maximize the expected patient survival rate. To address this, this study establishes a Markov Decision Process (MDP) model to make real-time decisions about ambulance dispatch, ambulance redeployment, and hospital selection based on the current state of the MCI system, optimizing resource allocation. Due to the high-dimensional and uncountable state space of this MDP model, and the inability to accurately estimate its transition probabilities, we propose a novel simulation-based approximate dynamic programming solution method, integrating a deep-neural-network-based approximate policy iteration (DNN-API) algorithm with a hybrid agent-based and discrete event simulation to efficiently generate near-optimal decisions. In collaboration with the National Science and Technology Center for Disaster Reduction in Taiwan, we conduct computational experiments using a potential earthquake scenario in Taipei City to assess the efficiency and effectiveness of our proposed simulation-based approximate dynamic programming algorithm compared to the least square time difference-based ADP method and current practice heuristics.

Title: Operational modes and logistical fulfillment options in the context of cross-border E-commerce platform services
Authors: Xuhui Chen, Yong He, Xiaoying Tang, Shibo Jin
Abstract: The rapid advancement of cross-border e-commerce has led to the emergence of platform self-operated channels and bonded warehouses, thereby establishing new service norms in this sector. This development presents overseas e-tailers with the opportunity to select more suitable operational modes and logistics fulfillment methods amidst increasing competition. However, for conventional direct-mail e-tailers, transitioning operational modes or logistics fulfillment methods can be risky due to demand (or sales volume) uncertainty under new channels, making it challenging to balance expected sales revenue against costs. To address this issue, we design a stochastic simulation framework to effectively support strategic decision-making. Specifically, we develop mathematical formulations for different modes aimed at quantifying expected profits to aid decision-making. A mixed-integer linear programming model is proposed for designing the most complex third-party bonded logistics network. Then, we design an enhanced Benders decomposition algorithm, augmented by multiple cuts, Pareto-optimal cuts, and warm-start, to solve the proposed model. The estimated demand distribution is generated using a compiled, freely available dataset obtained from the cross-border e-commerce platform via AI-supervised learning. A real-world case study is conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our model and method, providing actionable insights on strategic decision-making for overseas e-tailers through key parameter sensitivity analysis.

Title: Fixed-flexible mixed periodic vehicle routing problem with balancing the number of vehicles
Authors: Jian Li, Fuxin Zhou, Ruoxi Yang, Zhaotong Zhang, Yunfeng Ma, Panos M. Pardalos
Abstract: A new variant of periodic vehicle routing problem (VRP) is proposed in this study. Two additional factors are considered: (i) delivery flexibility by relaxing the fixed visit frequency and delivery quantity for some customers; (ii) balancing the number of vehicles over planning horizon to maintain stability in the usage of long-term leased vehicles and short-term leased vehicles. This problem simultaneously takes into account the fixed and flexible visit customers. A fixed-flexible mixed periodic VRP is proposed to comprehensively address these issues. Thereafter, a mixed integer programming model that includes several valid inequalities is established. We also designed a matheuristic approach in which a split-insert mathematical model is proposed to address the insertion decision problem. An iterated local search algorithm is used to obtain improved solutions. The split-insert mathematical model is proposed to use in the local search and perturbation phases of the iterated local search algorithm. The efficiency of the entire algorithm is evaluated by using the stochastically generated instances. Sensitivity experiments show that considering delivery flexibility can reduce the total cost within the planning horizon. After delivery flexibility reaches a certain level, it can reduce costs by more than 8.50%. However, further increases in flexibility lead to additional savings of less than 1%. Compared to maintaining a fixed fleet size, balancing the number of vehicles can achieve average total cost savings of 11.14% within the planning horizon. These findings can provide practical management insights for firms.

Title: Modeling flex-route transit systems with a continuous approximation Markovian approach
Authors: Carlos Olivos, Alexander Vinel, Daniel F. Silva
Abstract: This paper presents a performance evaluation framework for flex-route public transit systems that combines a fixed route with on-demand flexibility, allowing deviations for passenger pickups or drop-offs. We develop a Continuous Approximation Markov Process (CAMP) model that tracks checkpoint-to-checkpoint lateness as a discrete-time continuous-state Markov chain, with transition increments derived from a continuous approximation of travel-time distributions. Unlike most existing approaches, the model explicitly allows backtracking and incorporates delay-dependent request arrivals, capturing how delays propagate through successive checkpoints. This approach provides both steady-state and transient measures and allows for distributional metrics beyond the expected delay at each checkpoint, including the probability of being late, quantiles, and the standard deviation of delay. We benchmark the framework against simplified models that assume no backtracking, an exponential travel-time distribution, or deterministic averages. The comparison shows that these alternatives misestimate performance metrics, including delay variability and the probability of lateness. In the case of backtracking, considering this policy reduces route length by as much as 23%, and therefore results in substantially different system behavior. The proposed model provides a tool for assessing service reliability and supporting design decisions, such as selecting an appropriate schedule time in flex-route systems.

Title: Toward Industry 6.0: The Ecosystem Age, superintelligence, viability, and OR-AI symbiosis
Authors: Dmitry Ivanov
Abstract: Operations and supply chains have witnessed spectacular transformations through Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0. Is the next industrial revolution – Industry 6.0 – unfolding in the context of artificial intelligence (AI) and human-AI collaboration? And, possibly, even Industry 7.0 and superintelligence (SI) are just around the corner? In this paper, we conceptualize the transition toward Industry 6.0 as the Ecosystem Age that builds upon technologies developed in Industry 4.0 and viability-centric socio-ecological principles proposed in Industry 5.0, emerging into a cyber-socio-technical-ecological industrial revolution. We create a taxonomy of industrial revolutions based on the types of work that have been replaced/transformed by machines over time, and utilize it to delineate Industry 6.0 and forecast Industry 7.0 framed in technology (e.g., generative AI, agentic AI, edge AI, and humanoid robots), organization (i.e., decentralized, autonomous, agentic-driven planning and control), and modelling (OR-AI symbiosis) dimensions. Second, we discuss potential impacts of the transition toward Industry 6.0 on Operations Research (OR) with associated challenges and chances, outlining a 7-layer architecture of OR-AI symbiosis in digital twins. We elaborate on the technology and viability principles that frame Industry 6.0 and discuss scenarios for further transitioning toward next industrial revolutions and cyber-virtual, AI-driven networks that learn, adapt, self-organize, and regenerate. We conclude by outlining research opportunities for OR in the new era of supply chain and operations management in the AI and superintelligence age.

Title: Partially-supervised neural network model for quadratic multiparametric programming
Authors: Fuat Can Beylunioğlu, Mehrdad Pirnia, P. Robert Duimering
Abstract: Neural Networks (NN) with ReLU activation functions are used to model multiparametric quadratic optimization problems (mp-QP) in diverse engineering applications. Researchers have suggested leveraging the piecewise affine property of deep NN models to solve mp-QP with linear constraints, which also exhibit piecewise affine behaviour. However, traditional deep NN applications to mp-QP fall short of providing optimal and feasible predictions, even when trained on large datasets. This study proposes a partially-supervised NN (PSNN) architecture that directly represents the mathematical structure of the global solution function. In contrast to generic NN training approaches, the proposed PSNN method derives a large proportion of model weights directly from the mathematical properties of the optimization problem, producing more accurate solutions despite significantly smaller training data sets. Many energy management problems are formulated as QP, so we apply the proposed approach to energy systems (specifically DC optimal power flow) to demonstrate proof of concept. Model performance in terms of solution accuracy and speed of predictions was compared against a commercial solver and a generic Deep NN model based on classical training. Results show KKT sufficient conditions for PSNN consistently outperform generic NN architectures with classical training using far less data, including when tested on extreme, out-of-training distribution test data. Given its speed advantages over traditional solvers, the PSNN model can quickly produce optimal and feasible solutions within a second for millions of input parameters sampled from a distribution of stochastic demands and renewable generator dispatches, which can be used for simulations and long term planning.

Title: Direct delivery or buffered delivery? an efficient heuristic for the material delivery strategy selection problem
Authors: Jianbin Li, Wei Si, Qihuang Mei, Yue Wang
Abstract: To ensure stable material flow, manufacturing enterprises need to deliver raw materials from the central warehouse to production lines on time. Two delivery strategies are generally used: (1) the direct delivery (DD) strategy, where raw materials are delivered directly from the central warehouse to the production line as needed, and (2) the buffered delivery (BD) strategy, where raw materials are first sent to a supermarket near the production line for temporary storage before final delivery. However, improper strategy selection for a raw material distribution system may lead to high unpacking costs—since different strategies adopt distinct unpacking rules—along with long demand response times and low supermarket utilization. This study proposes a mixed-integer programming model to determine the selection of delivery strategies and the delivery quantities for raw materials in each delivery period.
